To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the proportion of diabetic patients with regular physical exercise increased significantly in both sexes after 1 year of intensified diet and exercise intervention, but 2) no significant increase in aerobic capacity was found, and 3) aerobic capacity and its change were inversely related to the level and change in HbAlc, and 4) the increase in aerobic capacity after 1 year was associated with a rise in HDL- cholesterol.
in middle-aged obese diabetic patients, a 12-month intensified diet and exercise programme was not sufficient to increase physical activity and aerobic fitness.

in middle-aged, newly-diagnosed patients with Type 2 (Non-insulin-dependent) Diabetes Mellitus, 1-year intensified dietary education, continuous encouragement and follow-up to increase physical activity, and assessment of the level and changes of aerobic capacity did not result in a significant increase in the amount of regular physical activity or in the improvement of aerobic capacity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of a one-year intensified diet and physical activity education programme on habitual physical activity, aerobic and metabolic control in middle-aged, non-insulin-dependent (Type 2) diabetic patients.

the effects of a long-term intensified diet and exercise programme on habitual physical activity, aerobic exercise capacity and metabolic control of diabetes in newly-diagnosed patients with Type 2 (formerly known as non-insulin-dependent) (NIID) diabetes mellitus.
the relationship between habitual physical activity and the metabolic control of newly-diagnosed non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study do not provide sufficient evidence for a positive effect of exercise on metabolic control in patients newly diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes.
the present study does not show any significant increase in physical exercise or aerobic capacity after 1 year of intensified education.

physical activity and aerobic exercise are important in the treatment of diabetes, but that more studies are needed to assess the most effective methods of increasing physical activity in diabetic patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aerobic capacity is a key factor for metabolic control in diabetic patients.
physical activity is a good way to improve aerobic capacity and metabolic profile in diabetic patients.
the patients who had the best metabolic control at the end of 1 year were those who had the highest aerobic capacity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aerobic capacity is associated to metabolic control of diabetes and HDL-cholestrol level.
exercise is a critical part of the treatment plan for people with Type 2 diabetes, and it should be a part of every patient’s treatment plan.
physical activity and exercise are important in diabetes care.
